messages:
leah: Heads up — Acme reported a p95 latency spike + intermittent 503s against hosted inference in eu-west-1 around 11:10–11:20 UTC. They included a minimal repro and a request-id. Posting what they sent below.

leah: ```bash
# customer curl
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \\n  -H 'X-Request-ID: r-abc123' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium-quant","prompt":"summarize...","max_tokens":1024}'
```

eng-oncall: Investigating now. I can already see elevated tail latencies across the proxy layer for eu-west-1, and a small rise in 5xx counters. Pulling traces for r-abc123.

mike: Can you paste the full X-Request-ID and the client SDK version from the customer? Also how many concurrent connections did they report?

leah: They say python-sdk v1.3.2, streaming generate, concurrency ~12 parallel requests from a worker pool. Request-ID exact: r-abc123 (same as header above). They also attached a short client log showing repeated 503s and immediate retries.

sre-bot: [alert] eu-west-1 gateway: 5xx rate +820% (11:08 -> 11:18 UTC). p95 latency spike to ~1.2s. See: https://monitoring.redwood.com/alerts/edge-eu-west-503-3456

juniper: Quick triage — looks like edge proxy queue growth + backend model pool exhaustion on nodes serving `gpt-medium-quant` (quantized variant). A few backend pods hit connection_queue > 1000 and started returning 503s. I'm going to flip routing to the fallback variant (non-quant) and bump backend pool size for eu-west.

eng-oncall: Sounds good. Mitigation plan: 1) route new traffic to `gpt-medium-fallback` (already compatible), 2) increase backend pool by +30% in eu-west autoscale group, 3) advise customer to lower concurrency to 6 while we stabilize.

juniper: Routing switch applied at 11:22 UTC. Autoscale policy adjusted (min replicas +2, scale window shortened). Watching metrics now.

eng-oncall: Temporary client-side workaround to recommend to customers: enable exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries to 3. Example (python):

```python
# backoff pseudo
import time, random
def call_with_backoff(fn):
    for i in range(3):
        try:
            return fn()
        except Exception as e:
            wait = (2 ** i) * 0.2 + random.uniform(0, 0.1)
            time.sleep(wait)
    raise
```

leah: I'll send CS note now: "We've routed your traffic to a fallback model and increased capacity in eu-west-1. Please try again with concurrency <=6 and client-side backoff. We'll follow up when autoscaling is stable." :thumbsup:

cs-escalations: Customer reply: "After your change we see immediate reduction in 503s and p95 dropped from ~1300ms to ~210ms. Thanks — will keep testing w/ lower concurrency."

mike: Please open an incident ticket for postmortem and assign to eng-runtime + infra. We should capture: potential qps threshold mis-tune for quant variant + autoscale responsiveness.

juniper: Autoscale finished at 11:35 UTC, backend queue lengths normalized, 5xx counts back to baseline. I'll file a PR to adjust per-node qps and lower threshold that triggers queue backpressure for quantized variants.

leah: Great. I'll close the customer loop and mark this thread for postmortem follow-up notes.

eng-oncall: Follow-up action items: [eng-runtime] tune qps thresholds, [infra] verify autoscale cooldown and scale delta, [sre] add a synthetic test hitting quantized path to catch regressions.

leah: Thanks everyone. I'll paste the customer-facing note in the ticket and leave it open until postmortem done. :white_check_mark:
